title: Lessons from the Bedok tuberculosis screening for hawker businesses
asked: Mr Pritam Singh asked what lessons were learned from the mandatory tuberculosis screening exercise announced at three Bedok locations on 30 April 2026, particularly its impact on the business prospects of high footfall places such as hawker centres and markets.
response: Mr Tan Kiat How said the Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) carries out ground operations such as the Bedok TB screening when needed, and that clear communication with residents is a key success factor because rumours spread without authoritative information. Eligible hawkers and tenants received rental and service and conservancy charge rebates to mitigate the temporary impact on their businesses, and partnerships between CDA, community stakeholders and grassroots organisations were described as critical. He said the 13 cases were spread over three years and none were hawkers, merchants or people working in Heartbeat@Bedok or Bedok Town, but everyone there was tested as a precaution. He said there are learning points on how the exercise could have been explained better, and that these will be incorporated into standard operating procedures.
